test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 18 and 9 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do twice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(3, 18, 9) = 18 units.

Combined efficiency = (18 ÷ 3) + (18 ÷ 18) + (18 ÷ 9) = 6 + 1 + 2 = 9 units/day.

Target work = 2 × Total work = 2 × 18 = 36 units.

Required time = Target work ÷ Combined efficiency = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 3 days

Time taken by B = 18 days

Time taken by C = 9 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Time

Time Taken = Target Work ÷ Total Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C together = 6 + 1 + 2 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Original Total Work = 18 units.

⇒ Work to be done = Twice the original work = 2 × 18 = 36 units.

⇒ Time taken to complete the new work = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by individuals. If everyone works for the same number of days, the total wages are simply distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept remains exactly the same as Time & Work. Filling pipes have positive efficiency, whereas emptying pipes or leaks have negative efficiency.

Alternate Day Work

When persons work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and multiply by a factor to get as close to the total work as possible without exceeding it.
